docs.title: Whisper ASR Webservice
docs.text: Whisper ASR Webservice is a self-hosted REST API for speech recognition, translation and language identification based on OpenAI Whisper. It runs as a Docker container on CPU or NVIDIA GPU.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• OpenAI-compatible API: works with the OpenAI SDKs and any application that lets you set the OpenAI base URL
  • Three engines: OpenAI Whisper, Faster Whisper and WhisperX
  • Transcription in every language Whisper supports, and translation into English
  • Language detection with a confidence score
  • Output as plain text, JSON, WebVTT, SRT or TSV
  • Word-level timestamps, voice activity detection (VAD) and speaker diarization
  • Accepts any audio or video file FFmpeg can decode, decoded in-process with PyAV
  • Optional API key authentication
  • Unloads the model when idle to free memory
  • Interactive API documentation (Swagger UI)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
CPUGPU 
docker run -d -p 9000:9000 \
  -e ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper \
  -e ASR_MODEL=base \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest

docker run -d --gpus all -p 9000:9000 \
  -e ASR_MODEL=base \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest-gpu

Open http://localhost:9000/docs to use the API from your browser, or send a request directly:

curl http://localhost:9000/v1/audio/transcriptions -F model=whisper-1 -F file=@audio.mp3

docs.title: Engines
docs.text: Engine ASR_ENGINE Notes OpenAI Whisper openai_whisper Reference implementation Faster Whisper faster_whisper (default) Faster and lighter on memory; VAD and batched inference WhisperX whisperx Word alignment and speaker diarization

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Report bugs and request features on GitHub Issues. For questions and discussion, join the Discord server.

docs.title: License
docs.text: Released under the MIT License. Audio is decoded with PyAV, which bundles FFmpeg libraries licensed under the LGPL v3.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or 3.13
  • uv
  • For GPU support, an NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 12.8 or newer

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text: The diagram source is request-flow.excalidraw, which can be opened and edited at excalidraw.com.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text: Path Responsibility app/webservice.py FastAPI application, endpoints, API key check and CLI entry point app/config.py Reads the environment variables app/utils.py Audio decoding with PyAV and the output format writers app/factory/asr_model_factory.py Creates the engine selected by ASR_ENGINE app/asr_models/asr_model.py Engine base class: model lock, lazy loading and idle unloading app/asr_models/*_engine.py openai_whisper, faster_whisper and whisperx implementations tests/ API and audio decoding tests

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv sync                                # CPU build of PyTorch
uv sync --no-group cpu --group cuda    # PyTorch for CUDA 12.8 (CUDA 12.9 on ARM64)

uv run installs the default CPU build again before running a command, so after installing the CUDA build run commands with uv run --no-sync, or set UV_NO_SYNC=1.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
uv run whisper-asr-webservice --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000

Configure the service with the environment variables, for example ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper ASR_MODEL=tiny uv run whisper-asr-webservice.

docs.title: Test and Lint
docs.text:
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check app tests

The tests replace the ASR engine with a stub, so they run without downloading models.

docs.title: Build Docker Images
docs.text:
CPUGPUDocker Compose 
docker build -t whisper-asr-webservice .
docker run -d -p 9000:9000 whisper-asr-webservice

docker build -f Dockerfile.gpu -t whisper-asr-webservice-gpu .
docker run -d --gpus all -p 9000:9000 whisper-asr-webservice-gpu

docker compose up --build                            # CPU
docker compose -f docker-compose.gpu.yml up --build  # GPU

The Compose files mount ./app into the container, so code changes take effect after a restart without a rebuild.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
uv run mkdocs serve

The site is served at http://localhost:8000 and reloads on changes.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Pushing a version tag publishes the Docker images, creates a GitHub release and deploys this documentation. Pushing to the debug branch publishes the debug and debug-gpu images for testing.

Each architecture is built on a native GitHub runner and scanned with Trivy before the multi-platform tags are published, so a failed scan never updates a published tag. The per-architecture images stay available as <tag>-amd64, <tag>-arm64, <tag>-gpu-amd64 and <tag>-gpu-arm64. Builds of the debug branch reuse the layer cache stored in the buildcache-* tags; version tags are always built from scratch.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• OpenAI-compatible API: /v1/audio/transcriptions, /v1/audio/translations and /v1/models, with every response format including verbose_json and diarized_json, word timestamps, streaming and OpenAI's error format, so the OpenAI SDKs and applications built for OpenAI work by changing the base URL
  • Authorization: Bearer authentication with API_KEY, next to the X-API-Key header
  • CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS to allow browser-based applications on other origins to call the API
  • ROOT_PATH to serve the service behind a reverse proxy under a path prefix, including the documentation and Swagger UI
  • ASR_VAD_THRESHOLD, ASR_VAD_MIN_SILENCE_MS and ASR_VAD_SPEECH_PAD_MS to tune voice activity detection; the threshold also applies to WhisperX, which drops the start or end of some non-English audio with its default
  • ASR_PROMPT_RESET_ON_TEMPERATURE to keep punctuation and capitalization on long recordings
  • ASR_CONDITION_ON_PREVIOUS_TEXT to stop Whisper from skipping speech at the end of a file, such as an outro after the main content
  • vad_filter for /detect-language, so the language is detected from speech instead of leading silence
  • ASR_CPU_THREADS to use more CPU cores; faster_whisper and whisperx use 4 threads by default
  • GPU Docker image for ARM64, e.g. NVIDIA DGX and Grace, with PyTorch built for CUDA 12.9; only the openai_whisper engine can use the GPU there, so it is the default on these systems

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
See the upgrade guide for what to check when upgrading from v1.

  • Docker images no longer include the ffmpeg binary; audio is decoded in-process with PyAV
  • /asr?output=json returns the same structure for every engine, following OpenAI's verbose_json format; language is now a name such as english
  • SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_WIDTH and SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_COUNT are unset by default, so subtitles contain one cue per segment
  • The default engine is faster_whisper instead of openai_whisper; set ASR_ENGINE=openai_whisper to keep the previous engine

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Audio is decoded in-process with PyAV instead of an ffmpeg subprocess, so running from source no longer requires FFmpeg
  • Removed the ffmpeg-python dependency and the FFmpeg build layer from the Docker images
  • All engines share one set of output writers, and the SUBTITLE_* settings apply to every engine
  • /asr and /detect-language are documented as the legacy API
  • The documentation explains how to run offline with cached models, including WhisperX
  • The documentation lists the distilled models and explains how to use custom and fine-tuned models
  • /detect-language no longer rounds the WhisperX confidence to two decimals
  • The project uses uv instead of Poetry: uv sync installs the CPU build of PyTorch, uv sync --no-group cpu --group cuda the CUDA build, and locking and Docker builds are much faster
  • The CPU Docker image no longer includes pip
  • The CPU Docker image is based on Debian 13 instead of Debian 12, which has far fewer known vulnerabilities

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• WhisperX subtitles missing the spaces between words, and merging many segments into one subtitle
  • word_timestamps missing from the Swagger UI with the openai_whisper engine, which supports it
  • Installing without extras failing on macOS and arm64 because the CUDA build of PyTorch was selected
  • Transcription with more than 4 CPU threads being several times slower because the model was loaded in a thread that exits

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• API test suite and a CI workflow running ruff and pytest
  • ASR_BEAM_SIZE, ASR_BATCH_SIZE and ASR_VAD_FILTER environment variables
  • MODEL_UNLOAD_AFTER_REQUEST environment variable to unload the model as soon as each request finishes
  • MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB and MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS limits that reject oversized uploads (413) and excess requests (503); both are off by default
  • /health endpoint for container health checks, public even when API_KEY is set
  • Docker images define a HEALTHCHECK that uses the /health endpoint
  • Docker images carry OCI labels: title, description, version, revision, creation time, license, documentation and source URLs
  • Logging with timestamps and a LOG_LEVEL setting: startup configuration, model loading and every request with its duration at INFO, and decoding times and engine options at DEBUG
  • Optional API key authentication with the API_KEY environment variable
  • GitHub release is created automatically when a version tag's Docker images are published successfully
  • Docker images can run as a non-root user (--user) with XDG_CACHE_HOME pointing to a writable cache directory; ASR_MODEL_PATH now defaults to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/whisper
  • Request flow diagram in the README and the development guide
  • Trivy vulnerability scans on pull requests and before publishing images: fixable HIGH/CRITICAL findings fail the pipeline, MEDIUM findings produce a warning
  • Per-architecture Docker image tags (<version>-amd64, <version>-arm64, <version>-gpu-amd64); arm64 images are built on native runners instead of under emulation

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The service starts accepting connections immediately and loads the model in the background; /health returns 503 with {"status": "loading"} until the model is ready, and requests sent meanwhile wait for it
  • Upgraded
  • Python requirement to >=3.12,<3.14
  • Poetry to v2.5.2
  • PyTorch to v2.8.0 (CUDA builds now use CUDA 12.8, adding RTX 50xx / Blackwell sm_120 support)
  • whisperx to v3.8.6 and pyannote-audio to v4.1.1
  • fastapi to v0.165.0
  • uvicorn to v0.54.0
  • python-multipart to v0.0.34
  • tqdm to v4.70.1
  • llvmlite to v0.50.0
  • numba to v0.68.1
  • GitHub Actions to their latest major versions
  • WhisperX diarization now uses pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1; accept its conditions on Hugging Face
  • Only the selected ASR engine is imported at startup, reducing startup time and memory use
  • Docker images use the FFmpeg n9.1 build layer
  • Refreshed locked dependencies to pick up security fixes (aiohttp, certifi, filelock, lightning, nltk, pillow, urllib3 and more)
  • CPU Docker image is based on python:3.12-slim-bookworm
  • Docker images include the FFmpeg license (LGPL v2.1+) at /usr/local/share/doc/ffmpeg
  • Docker images no longer include development dependencies, and dependencies are installed in their own layer so rebuilds after code changes are faster
  • Docker images are built in a separate stage and no longer contain Poetry, its dependencies or download caches, making them several GB smaller
  • Rewrote the README and documentation, adding the API reference, a complete configuration table and the development guide

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Model being unloaded right after a request that took longer than MODEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT
  • WhisperX crash loop at startup (Weights only load failed) caused by lightning 2.6 with pyannote-audio 3.x
  • Model failing to reload after MODEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT unloaded it, especially with WhisperX
  • initial_prompt causing HTTP 500 with the WhisperX engine
  • WhisperX diarization ignoring min_speakers and max_speakers
  • /detect-language returning the confidence of the wrong language with the openai_whisper engine
  • Empty transcripts for M4A/MP4/MOV files that store their index at the end of the file
  • Undecodable, empty or malformed raw (encode=false) uploads now return HTTP 400
  • /asr responses now use a Content-Type matching the requested output format
  • Swagger UI showing a text field instead of a file picker for audio_file in Docker images
  • Server becoming unresponsive, including /docs, while a transcription is running
  • Missing contact URL in the OpenAPI metadata

docs.title: Legacy API
docs.text:
These are the service's original endpoints. They remain supported for existing integrations; new integrations should use the OpenAI-compatible API. Both accept a file upload as multipart/form-data in the audio_file field. Interactive documentation is available at /docs, and the OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json.

Method Path Description POST /asr Transcribe or translate an audio file POST /detect-language Detect the spoken language of an audio file

docs.title: Transcription
docs.text:
POST /asr

Transcribes the uploaded file in its original language, or translates it into English.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description audio_file file required Audio or video file task string transcribe transcribe or translate (into English) language string auto-detected Language code of the audio, e.g. en, de, tr output string txt txt, json, vtt, srt or tsv initial_prompt string none Text that guides the style or vocabulary of the transcript encode boolean true Decode the file. Set to false to send raw PCM (see below) word_timestamps boolean false Include word-level timestamps. openai_whisper and faster_whisper vad_filter boolean false Skip parts of the audio without speech. faster_whisper only diarize boolean false Label segments by speaker. whisperx only, requires HF_TOKEN min_speakers integer none Lower bound on the number of speakers. whisperx only max_speakers integer none Upper bound on the number of speakers. whisperx only

All parameters except audio_file are query parameters. Some engine-specific parameters are hidden in the Swagger UI when a different engine is configured.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Plain text transcript
curl -F "audio_file=@meeting.mp3" "http://localhost:9000/asr"

# SRT subtitles for a video
curl -F "audio_file=@video.mp4" "http://localhost:9000/asr?output=srt" -o video.srt

# English translation of German audio
curl -F "audio_file=@interview.wav" "http://localhost:9000/asr?task=translate&language=de"

# Speaker diarization with WhisperX
curl -F "audio_file=@call.m4a" "http://localhost:9000/asr?output=json&diarize=true&max_speakers=2"

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
output Content type Description txt text/plain Plain transcript json application/json Full result with segments, timestamps and metadata vtt text/vtt WebVTT subtitles srt application/x-subrip SubRip subtitles tsv text/tab-separated-values Segment start, end (in milliseconds) and text

The JSON output has the same structure for every engine and follows OpenAI's verbose_json format:

  • task: transcribe or translate
  • language: the detected or requested language, as a lowercase name such as english
  • duration: the length of the audio in seconds
  • text: the full transcript
  • segments: one entry per segment with id, seek, start, end, text, tokens, temperature, avg_logprob, compression_ratio and no_speech_prob, plus speaker when diarization is enabled. WhisperX does not report the decoding statistics, so they are 0 with that engine.
  • words: word timestamps with word, start, end and probability, included when word_timestamps is enabled or with the WhisperX engine

With diarization, the text outputs prefix every segment with its speaker, e.g. [SPEAKER_00]: Hello.

The response includes an Asr-Engine header with the engine that produced it.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
With encode=true (the default), any audio or video format supported by FFmpeg is accepted, including MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, Opus, M4A, MP4, MOV, MKV and WebM. The file is decoded in-process with PyAV and converted to 16 kHz mono before transcription.

With encode=false, the file must be raw 16-bit little-endian mono PCM at 16 kHz. This skips decoding and is useful when the client already has decoded audio.

docs.title: Language Detection
docs.text:
POST /detect-language

Detects the language spoken in the first 30 seconds of the file, or of its speech with vad_filter=true.

Name Type Default Description audio_file file required Audio or video file encode boolean true Decode the file vad_filter boolean false Detect from speech, skipping silence. faster_whisper only 
curl -F "audio_file=@audio.mp3" "http://localhost:9000/detect-language"

{
  "detected_language": "english",
  "language_code": "en",
  "confidence": 0.98
}

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
The service starts accepting connections right away and loads the model in the background. Until the model is loaded, GET /health returns 503 with {"status": "loading"}, and /asr and /detect-language requests wait for the model. Afterwards it returns {"status": "ok"}. It does not require the API key, so container orchestrators and load balancers can use it.

curl http://localhost:9000/health

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
When the API_KEY environment variable is set, both endpoints require the key in the X-API-Key header or as Authorization: Bearer <key>. The documentation pages stay public, and the Swagger UI provides an Authorize button to enter the key.

curl -H "X-API-Key: your-secret-key" -F "audio_file=@audio.mp3" "http://localhost:9000/asr"

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Cause 400 The file could not be decoded or contains no audio 401 API_KEY is set and the X-API-Key header is missing or wrong 413 The upload is larger than MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB 422 A parameter has an invalid value, e.g. an unknown output or language 503 MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS requests are already being processed or waiting

Error responses are JSON objects with a detail field describing the problem, except 413, which is plain text.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The service is configured with environment variables. All of them are optional.

Variable Default Description ASR_ENGINE faster_whisper faster_whisper, openai_whisper or whisperx; openai_whisper by default on ARM64 GPUs ASR_MODEL base Model to load, see Models ASR_MODEL_PATH $XDG_CACHE_HOME/whisper Model download directory (openai_whisper, faster_whisper) XDG_CACHE_HOME ~/.cache Base directory for downloaded models and data ASR_DEVICE cuda if available, else cpu Device to run the model on ASR_CPU_THREADS engine default CPU threads for transcription, see Device and Quantization ASR_QUANTIZATION float32 on GPU, int8 on CPU Weight precision (faster_whisper, whisperx) ASR_BEAM_SIZE engine default Beam size used for decoding ASR_BATCH_SIZE engine default Batch size for batched inference (faster_whisper, whisperx) ASR_VAD_FILTER false Default value of the vad_filter request parameter ASR_VAD_THRESHOLD engine default Speech probability threshold of the VAD, see Voice Activity Detection ASR_VAD_MIN_SILENCE_MS engine default Silence length that ends a speech segment (faster_whisper) ASR_VAD_SPEECH_PAD_MS engine default Padding added around speech segments (faster_whisper) ASR_CONDITION_ON_PREVIOUS_TEXT engine default Use the previous text as context for the next window, see Decoding ASR_PROMPT_RESET_ON_TEMPERATURE engine default Reset the prompt above this fallback temperature (faster_whisper, whisperx) MODEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT 0 Seconds of inactivity before the model is unloaded; 0 keeps it loaded MODEL_UNLOAD_AFTER_REQUEST false Unload the model after every request, see Model Unloading API_KEY unset Require this key in the X-API-Key request header HF_TOKEN unset Hugging Face token for WhisperX diarization SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_WIDTH unset Maximum characters per subtitle line, see Subtitles SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_COUNT unset Maximum lines per subtitle, see Subtitles SUBTITLE_HIGHLIGHT_WORDS false Underline the current word in subtitles, see Subtitles SAMPLE_RATE 16000 Sample rate audio is converted to. Whisper expects 16 kHz MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB 0 Largest accepted upload in MB; 0 means no limit, see Limits MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS 0 Requests processed or waiting at once; 0 means no limit CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS unset Comma-separated origins allowed to call the API from a browser ROOT_PATH unset URL prefix when served behind a reverse proxy, e.g. /whisper LOG_LEVEL INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR, see Logging

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Type Models Multilingual tiny, base, small, medium, large-v1, large-v2, large-v3 (large), large-v3-turbo (turbo) English only tiny.en, base.en, small.en, medium.en Distilled distil-small.en, distil-medium.en, distil-large-v2, distil-large-v3, distil-large-v3.5 (faster_whisper, whisperx)

Larger models are more accurate but slower and need more memory. turbo is close to large-v3 in accuracy at a fraction of the cost and is a good default on GPU. For English-only audio, the .en models are more accurate than their multilingual counterparts, especially at the tiny and base sizes.

The distilled models are several times faster than the model they are distilled from, and the large ones stay within about 1% word error rate of it. They transcribe English only and cannot translate. distil-large-v2 is distilled from large-v2, and distil-large-v3 and distil-large-v3.5 from large-v3.

docs.title: Custom Models
docs.text:
With faster_whisper and whisperx, ASR_MODEL also accepts the Hugging Face repository id of a model converted to the CTranslate2 format, or the path to a local directory with such a model. With openai_whisper, it accepts the path to a model checkpoint (.pt file):

export ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper
export ASR_MODEL=Systran/faster-distil-whisper-large-v3

Models fine-tuned with Hugging Face transformers can be converted with ct2-transformers-converter.

docs.title: Device and Quantization
docs.text:
ASR_QUANTIZATION sets the precision of the model weights for faster_whisper and whisperx:

Value Speed Accuracy Notes float32 slowest highest Default on GPU float16 faster high Recommended on GPU int8 fastest lower Default on CPU

On a CPU, faster_whisper and whisperx use 4 threads by default. ASR_CPU_THREADS changes this, but more threads are not always faster, for example on CPUs that mix performance and efficiency cores, so measure with your own audio before changing it. On a CPU, ASR_BATCH_SIZE usually speeds up long files more than extra threads.

docs.title: Decoding
docs.text:
ASR_BEAM_SIZE and ASR_BATCH_SIZE tune decoding. When they are not set, each engine uses its own default.

With faster_whisper, setting ASR_BATCH_SIZE (for example 8) enables batched inference, which transcribes long files considerably faster on both GPU and CPU. Batched inference always applies voice activity detection to split the audio and does not use the previous text as context.

Whisper transcribes in 30-second windows and passes the text of the previous window to the next one as context. This keeps the style consistent, but it can also make the model stop too early, for example skipping speech at the end of a file after the main content, or lose punctuation and capitalization over time. ASR_CONDITION_ON_PREVIOUS_TEXT=false turns the context off (WhisperX already does this by default). A softer option is lowering ASR_PROMPT_RESET_ON_TEMPERATURE (default 0.5), for example to 0.3, which resets the context only when decoding becomes uncertain.

docs.title: Voice Activity Detection
docs.text:
Voice activity detection (VAD) skips the parts of the audio without speech. ASR_VAD_FILTER=true enables it by default for faster_whisper; clients can still override it per request with the vad_filter parameter, which /detect-language also accepts so the language is detected from speech instead of leading silence or music.

The VAD settings tune where speech starts and ends:

  • ASR_VAD_THRESHOLD: speech probability above which audio counts as speech (default 0.5). Lower it if quiet speech is skipped. With whisperx, it sets both the onset and offset of WhisperX's VAD, which is always on; values around 0.1 help when WhisperX drops the start or end of non-English audio.
  • ASR_VAD_MIN_SILENCE_MS: how long a silence must be to end a speech segment.
  • ASR_VAD_SPEECH_PAD_MS: padding added around each speech segment.

OpenAI API clients can set the same values per request with chunking_strategy, see OpenAI API.

docs.title: Model Unloading
docs.text:
When MODEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT is greater than 0, the model is unloaded after that many seconds without requests, which frees CPU or GPU memory. It is loaded again on the next request, which then takes longer to complete.

With MODEL_UNLOAD_AFTER_REQUEST=true, the model is unloaded as soon as each request finishes, so it only uses memory while a request is processed. Every request then includes the model loading time. This suits occasional use on a machine that needs its memory for other work.

docs.title: Subtitles
docs.text: By default, the srt and vtt outputs contain one subtitle per segment. Set both SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_WIDTH and SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_COUNT to split them into lines of at most that many characters instead, and SUBTITLE_HIGHLIGHT_WORDS=true to underline each word as it is spoken. Both need word timestamps, so enable word_timestamps or use the WhisperX engine, which always provides them.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The model processes one request at a time, and every request waiting for it keeps its decoded audio in memory (about 230 MB per hour of audio). On a shared or public server, set limits so that load cannot exhaust the memory:

export MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB=500       # larger uploads are rejected with 413 while they are being received
export MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS=4       # further requests are rejected with 503 until one finishes

Both limits are off by default.

docs.title: Browser Clients and Reverse Proxies
docs.text:
Browser-based applications can only call the API from another origin when that origin is allowed. List the origins in CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS, for example CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS=https://app.example.com,http://localhost:3000, or * to allow every origin.

When a reverse proxy serves the service under a path prefix and removes the prefix before forwarding requests, set ROOT_PATH to that prefix (e.g. ROOT_PATH=/whisper) so that redirects, the documentation and the Swagger UI use the right URLs.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
At INFO, the service logs its configuration at startup, model loading and unloading, and one line per request with the file name, audio length and processing time. Set LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG to also log all settings, audio decoding times, the options passed to the engine and the detected language, plus the health check requests that are hidden otherwise.

docker run -d -p 9000:9000 -e LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: When API_KEY is set, all API endpoints return 401 Unauthorized unless the request includes the key, either as Authorization: Bearer <key> or in the X-API-Key header. The documentation pages and /health remain public.

docs.title: Speaker Diarization
docs.text:
Diarization is available with the whisperx engine and requires a Hugging Face access token:

  1. Create a token at https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens.
  2. Accept the user conditions of pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 with the same account.
  3. Start the service with ASR_ENGINE=whisperx and HF_TOKEN=<your token>.

The diarize, min_speakers and max_speakers request parameters then become available.

docs.title: Upgrading to v2
docs.text: Version 2 adds an OpenAI-compatible API and keeps the original /asr and /detect-language endpoints, their parameters, the environment variables and the X-API-Key header. Most setups keep working unchanged; check the points below.

docs.title: Default Engine
docs.text:
The default engine is now faster_whisper, which is several times faster than openai_whisper with the same models. Transcripts can differ slightly in wording and punctuation. To keep the previous engine, set it explicitly:

-e ASR_ENGINE=openai_whisper

docs.title: JSON Output of /asr
docs.text:
/asr?output=json now returns the same structure for every engine, following OpenAI's verbose_json format. The txt, vtt, srt and tsv outputs and /detect-language are unchanged.

Before Now language as a code, e.g. en language as a name, e.g. english Segments as arrays with faster_whisper Segments as objects with named fields for every engine word_segments and score with whisperx words with word, start, end and probability Words inside each segment Words in a top-level words list — task and duration

See Output Formats for the full structure.

docs.title: Subtitles
docs.text: srt and vtt outputs contain one subtitle per segment by default with every engine. Before, WhisperX merged segments into longer subtitles. To split subtitles into lines, set SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_WIDTH and SUBTITLE_MAX_LINE_COUNT, see Subtitles.

docs.title: FFmpeg
docs.text: Audio is now decoded inside the service with PyAV, so the Docker images no longer contain the ffmpeg command and running from source no longer needs FFmpeg installed. Supported formats are unchanged.

docs.title: Running from Source
docs.text: The project uses uv instead of Poetry. uv sync installs the CPU build of PyTorch and the development tools; for NVIDIA GPUs use uv sync --no-group cpu --group cuda and then uv run --no-sync so that the CUDA build is kept. Run commands with uv run, e.g. uv run whisper-asr-webservice.

docs.title: New Integrations
docs.text: New integrations should use the OpenAI-compatible API: it works with the OpenAI SDKs and with applications that let you set the OpenAI base URL.

docs.title: OpenAI-Compatible API
docs.text:
The service implements OpenAI's speech-to-text API under /v1, so applications and libraries built for OpenAI can use it by changing the base URL to http://localhost:9000/v1.

Method Path Description POST /v1/audio/transcriptions Transcribe an audio file POST /v1/audio/translations Translate an audio file into English GET /v1/models List the available models GET /v1/models/{model} Retrieve a model

docs.title: Examples
Request Fields
docs.text:
Field Support file Any audio or video format FFmpeg can decode model Required, but any value is accepted: the request is served by the model set with ASR_MODEL language ISO-639-1 code such as en; region suffixes (en-US) and names (english) also work languages[] One language is used like language; several fall back to automatic detection prompt, keywords[] Passed to the model as initial prompt; keywords are appended to the prompt response_format json (default), text, srt, vtt, verbose_json, diarized_json timestamp_granularities[] segment (default) and word, with response_format=verbose_json temperature Sampling temperature between 0 and 1 stream Server-sent events, see Streaming chunking_strategy auto or a server_vad object enables voice activity detection (faster_whisper); its threshold, silence_duration_ms and prefix_padding_ms set the VAD settings for the request include[], known_speaker_names[], known_speaker_references[] Accepted and ignored

/v1/audio/translations accepts file, model, prompt, response_format (without diarized_json) and temperature, and always returns English text.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
• json: {"text": "...", "usage": {"type": "duration", "seconds": 11}}
  • text, srt, vtt: plain text
  • verbose_json: task, language, duration, text, segments, words (with the word granularity) and usage, the same structure as the /asr JSON output
  • diarized_json: segments labelled with speakers A, B, ... Requires ASR_ENGINE=whisperx and HF_TOKEN, see Speaker Diarization

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
With stream=true, the response is a stream of server-sent events: a transcript.text.delta event per segment, transcript.text.segment events with speakers for diarized_json, and a final transcript.text.done event with the full text. With faster_whisper, segments are sent as soon as they are transcribed; the other engines send them when the whole file is done.

stream = client.audio.transcriptions.create(model="whisper-1", file=audio, stream=True)
for event in stream:
    if event.type == "transcript.text.delta":
        print(event.delta, end="", flush=True)

docs.title: Errors and Authentication
docs.text: Errors use OpenAI's format, {"error": {"message": ..., "type": ..., "param": ..., "code": ...}}, so the OpenAI libraries raise their usual exceptions. When API_KEY is set, send it as Authorization: Bearer <key>; the X-API-Key header works as well.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text:
Any application that lets you set an OpenAI base URL for speech-to-text can use the service. For example:

  • Open WebUI: in Admin Settings → Audio, choose the OpenAI speech-to-text engine, set the API base URL to http://<host>:9000/v1 and the model to whisper-1.
  • LiteLLM: add a model with model: openai/whisper-1 and api_base: http://<host>:9000/v1.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The service is published on Docker Hub as onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice.

Tag Platforms Description latest linux/amd64, linux/arm64 Latest release, CPU latest-gpu linux/amd64, linux/arm64 Latest release, NVIDIA GPU <version> linux/amd64, linux/arm64 A specific release, CPU <version>-gpu linux/amd64, linux/arm64 A specific release, NVIDIA GPU

Pin a version tag (for example v1.11.0) in production so that upgrades happen only when you choose. All releases are listed on the releases page.

docs.title: CPU
docs.text:
docker run -d -p 9000:9000 \
  -e ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper \
  -e ASR_MODEL=base \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest

The CPU image also runs on Apple Silicon. Docker on macOS cannot access the GPU, so containers there always run on the CPU.

docs.title: GPU
docs.text:
docker run -d --gpus all -p 9000:9000 \
  -e ASR_MODEL=base \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest-gpu

Requirements:

  • An NVIDIA driver that supports CUDA 12.8 or newer
  • The NVIDIA Container Toolkit

The GPU image also runs on ARM64 systems such as NVIDIA DGX and Grace, but only the openai_whisper engine can use the GPU there: faster_whisper and whisperx are built on CTranslate2, which has no CUDA support for ARM64. The ARM64 image uses PyTorch built for CUDA 12.9, the only CUDA version PyTorch publishes for ARM64. On these systems the image uses openai_whisper by default, so leave out ASR_ENGINE or set it to openai_whisper. NVIDIA Jetson devices are not supported.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
services:
  whisper:
    image: onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest-gpu
    environment:
      - ASR_ENGINE=faster_whisper
      - ASR_MODEL=large-v3
      - MODEL_IDLE_TIMEOUT=300
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"
    volumes:
      - whisper-cache:/root/.cache
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu]

volumes:
  whisper-cache:

For the CPU image, use the latest tag and remove the deploy section.

docs.title: Model Cache
docs.text:
Models are downloaded on first start. Large models can take several minutes to download, so mount a volume at /root/.cache to keep them between container restarts:

docker run -d -p 9000:9000 \
  -v $PWD/cache:/root/.cache \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest

Note

Cached models are not re-downloaded, so you will not receive upstream model updates until you clear the cache.

docs.title: Running Offline
docs.text:
Once the models are in the cache, the service can run without internet access. Set HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 so that the Hugging Face libraries load the models from the cache instead of checking for updates online:

docker run -d -p 9000:9000 \
  -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  -v $PWD/cache:/root/.cache \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest

Start the service once with internet access first, so that it downloads the model. With WhisperX, also send one request for every language you need, because WhisperX downloads an alignment model per language on first use.

docs.title: Running as a Non-Root User
docs.text:
The images run as root by default, so existing setups and /root/.cache volumes keep working unchanged. To run as another user, set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a directory that user can write and mount the cache there:

mkdir -p cache
docker run -d -p 9000:9000 \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e XDG_CACHE_HOME=/cache \
  -v $PWD/cache:/cache \
  onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice:latest
  • All engines store their models and other downloaded data under XDG_CACHE_HOME.
  • To reuse a cache created by a container running as root, change its owner first, e.g. sudo chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" cache.
  • Do not make the cache writable by everyone (chmod 777). NLTK, which WhisperX uses for word alignment, refuses to load data from such a directory and the request fails. Change the owner as above instead.
  • Rootless Docker and rootless Podman need no extra options.
  • In Docker Compose, set user: "1000:1000" and the XDG_CACHE_HOME environment variable on the service. In Kubernetes, set runAsUser and runAsNonRoot: true in the pod's securityContext.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text: Once the container is running, open http://localhost:9000/docs to see the interactive API documentation.
